I've also completely lost interest in walking by the lake or building my model cars, so I just lie on the couch staring at the TV.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel excessively guilty about things you've done or haven't done, or do you ruminate on thoughts that you're worthless or a failure?\n\nPatient: Yeah, I feel like a complete screwup all the time. I keep blaming myself for losing my hours at work, telling myself I'm just lazy and useless. I constantly replay every mistake I've ever made, like it's proof I don't deserve anything better.\n\nDoctor: How long have you been experiencing these feelings of sadness, emptiness, and guilt, and have they been continuous or have you had any periods where you felt somewhat better?\n\nPatient: These feelings of sadness and guilt have been coming and going for several months, but they got much worse over the last month after my hours were cut. It hasn't been continuous, because I had a brief stretch recently where I suddenly felt unusually energetic and on top of the world before crashing back down into this heavy fog.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about that brief period where you felt unusually energetic and on top of the world, how long did it last and what was different about it compared to your usual state?\n\nPatient: Right after my hours got cut, I had a stretch for a few days where I felt on top of the world and was convinced I could easily start my own handyman business. I only slept about three hours a night but felt totally wired, with my thoughts racing so fast and my words coming out so quickly that my cousin couldn't even get a word in. It was the complete opposite of how I usually am, and nothing like this heavy fog I'm stuck in now.\n\nDoctor: During that brief period where you felt unusually energetic and on top of the world, did you engage in any impulsive or reckless behaviors, such as excessive spending or risky actions?\n\nPatient: No, I didn't really do anything reckless or spend money because my budget was already so tight. I had big ideas in my head, like buying a truck for the handyman work, but I didn't actually act on them or buy anything.\n\nDoctor: Can you estimate how many days that period of feeling unusually energetic and on top of the world lasted, and was it immediately followed by this crash into feeling sad and empty?\n\nPatient: That high, energetic period only lasted for about three or four days right after my hours got cut. As soon as that energy faded, I crashed straight into this heavy, sad, and empty feeling, and it's been dragging me down for the last few weeks.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm if there have been any other periods similar to that three or four-day stretch of feeling unusually energetic and on top of the world, or was this a one-time occurrence?\n\nPatient: No, that was a one-time thing that happened about a month ago right after my hours were cut. While I've had bouts of depression coming and going for several months before that, I've never experienced another period where I felt that unusually energetic or high.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any other episodes of feeling unusually energetic or 'high' like that one time, or has this been the only instance, and are you currently experiencing any symptoms of depression or mania?\n\nPatient: No, that was the only time I've ever felt high like that. Right now, I'm not feeling energetic at all; I'm in a severe low, feeling incredibly depressed, foggy, and drained. This deep crash has been really bad for the past month, though milder versions of this sadness have been coming and going for several months before that.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other episodes of significant mood elevation, even if not as intense as the one you described, or has your mood primarily been characterized by these depressive episodes?\n\nPatient: My mood has definitely been characterized by those depressive episodes, which have been coming and going for several months now. That high spell last month was a completely new and unusual experience for me, and I've never had any other periods of feeling elevated like that before.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned that the period of feeling unusually energetic and on top of the world lasted for about three or four days, but can you confirm if you've had any shorter periods, even just a day, where you felt significantly elevated or irritable since that time?\n\nPatient: No, since that one high spell, I haven't had any other days where I felt elevated or irritable at all. Instead, I've just been completely stuck in this heavy, drained state and unable to pull myself out of it.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced at least two episodes of feeling unusually energetic or 'high' in your lifetime, or was the episode you described a singular event?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure if I've had other times like that in the past, and I haven't really thought about it much. I can only clearly remember this recent one because of how much it stood out after my hours got cut.\n\nDoctor: Can you think back to any other times in your life, before this recent episode, where you might have felt unusually energetic, irritable, or 'high' for even a short period, even if it seems insignificant now?\n\nPatient: I can't really recall any other times of feeling unusually high or energetic before that stretch after my hours were cut. I've definitely had periods of depression in the past, but that was the only time I ever felt that kind of high.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any periods of feeling unusually energetic or 'high' that lasted less than four days, which might not have been as noticeable as the episode you described after your hours were cut?\n\nPatient: I don't really remember or haven't noticed any other times like that besides the one major stretch after my hours were cut. If I did have any shorter periods of feeling high like that, they didn't stand out to me at all.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm whether you have experienced at least two episodes of hypomania, which are periods of abnormally elevated or irritable mood that last at least four consecutive days, or was the episode you described a singular event in your lifetime?\n\nPatient: I’m really not sure if I’ve had other periods like that before. I can only clearly remember this recent high spell that happened right after my hours were cut, so anything else is hard to recall.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods of elevated mood or increased energy that lasted less than four days but were still noticeable to you or those around you, which might help clarify whether this recent episode was an isolated event or part of a pattern?\n\nPatient: Yes, that brief stretch of a few days right after my hours were cut was definitely noticeable. I felt unusually high, energized, and confident—staying up almost all night, pacing, talking fast, and making big plans that my cousin definitely noticed before I crashed into this deep depression.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any other times in your life where you had periods of elevated mood or increased energy that might have been shorter than four days but still stood out, even if they seem insignificant compared to the episode after your hours were cut?\n\nPatient: I don't really recall any other specific times like that before this recent period. My head is just so foggy right now that it's really hard to think back and remember much else.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other periods of elevated mood, increased energy, or decreased need for sleep that lasted less than four days but were still noticeable, either before or after the episode that occurred when your work hours were cut?\n\nPatient: I don't really remember having other high or energetic periods like that before. Usually, it was just the down, depressed feelings that came and went.\n\nDoctor: Can you think back to any times in your life when you might have had even shorter periods of feeling unusually energetic, confident, or 'high', even if they didn't last as long as the episode after your hours were cut?\n\nPatient: I'm really not sure, and I can't recall any other specific times like that before this past month. With my head being so foggy right now, it's just really hard to remember much of anything else.\n\nDoctor: To confirm, you've only clearly remembered one episode of feeling unusually energetic and 'high' that lasted a few days, but can you think of any other times, no matter how brief, where you felt significantly elevated or different from your usual self before this recent episode?\n\nPatient: I really can't recall any other times of feeling unusually energetic or high before that recent stretch. Before this, my struggles were mainly periods of deep, dragging depression that came and went over several months. That high spell was a completely new and different experience for me.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced at least two episodes of hypomania, which are periods of abnormally elevated or irritable mood that last at least four consecutive days, or was the episode you described a singular event in your lifetime, to help clarify whether you might be experiencing a bipolar disorder or another condition?\n\nPatient: I'm not entirely sure if I've had another full episode like that in the past. I only really noticed this recent high spell clearly after my hours got cut, though my mood has definitely had its ups and downs before.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm if you have experienced at least two episodes of hypomania in your lifetime, which are periods of abnormally elevated or irritable mood that last at least four consecutive days, to help differentiate between bipolar II disorder, major depressive disorder, and persistent depressive disorder?\n\nPatient: I'm really not sure and I don't recall having any other periods like that besides the recent one I described. My head is just too foggy to think back, so I can only remember that one time after my hours were cut.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any other periods of abnormally elevated or irritable mood, even if they didn't last as long as the episode after your hours were cut, that might help clarify whether you're experiencing bipolar II disorder or another condition?\n\nPatient: I really don't recall having any other periods of feeling abnormally high or irritable like that recent one. I've only really had those periods of deep depression that have been coming and going for several months.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any other times in your life where you might have had symptoms similar to that recent high spell, but perhaps less intense or shorter in duration, which could help us understand your condition better?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure and I can't recall any other specific times in my life where I felt that way.
